body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Ran an accessibility scan on {{domain}} and found {{total_issues}} WCAG 2.1 AA violations. For a SaaS company, this isn't just a legal risk — it's a direct revenue blocker. Enterprise buyers now require VPATs (Voluntary Product Accessibility Templates) as part of procurement, and your current state would fail any evaluation.

Three most urgent on {{business_name}}:

1. {{top_issue_1}} — your onboarding and signup flows have structural accessibility gaps. Every unlabeled form field or broken keyboard navigation is a potential user who can't complete setup — and a churn signal that never shows up in your metrics.

2. {{top_issue_2}} — dashboard components relying on color-only indicators (status badges, health checks, alert states) fail WCAG 1.4.1. Your 10% of color-blind users are making decisions with incomplete information.

3. {{top_issue_3}} — complex UI patterns (modals, dropdowns, data tables) without proper ARIA roles break screen-reader navigation entirely. This means assistive-technology users literally cannot operate your product.

The business case is clear: Gartner estimates that 80% of B2B SaaS will require accessibility compliance by 2027 for enterprise sales. Companies that get ahead of this win deals that competitors can't.

I can send {{business_name}} a free 17-point audit (with developer-ready remediation code). No commitment. Full implementation: $1,200 flat, 2 weeks.

Worth 15 minutes to see how you stack up?

— Emilio Ranucoli
Systems Engineer — accessibility & compliance audits
